scenes.title: 같은 길이인데 둔해 보이는 동작
lines: Both kicks extend quickly, but one feels sharp while the other seems to glide. If the attack arrives at the same time, where does that difference come from? The attacker kicks high and Lili rises into the air. Compare the extended foot at contact with the bent knee just before it. We'll change the timing of a kick and the path a fist takes home to see how interpolation affects rhythm. Interpolation calculates intermediate values between two values you've set. Set a bent arm and a straight arm, and the tool fills in the motion between them. A hand passing through the body is an obvious error. A technically clean motion that loses its force is easier to miss. This often shows up when strong poses drawn in 2D are translated into 3D. Even with the same poses and duration, extra in-betweens can take up most of the motion and weaken its impact. In Kula’s jump, her hair and knees change position markedly. The distinct sprite drawings make the rhythm easy to see.

scenes.title: 여덟 프레임 안의 시간 배분
lines: In our comparison, the attack arrives in eight frames. A frame is one division of time. At sixty frames per second, eight frames last about 0.13 seconds. With the total time fixed, compare how long each pose stays visible. The first version extends the bent leg at evenly spaced intervals. The second holds the preparation, then passes quickly through the middle into the strike. They arrive together, but we see different proportions of the important shapes. As Lili draws her kicking foot back, her whole body moves at different speeds. Watch how long the extended leg reads. Quickness can change without shortening the whole move. Keep the comparison conditions alike. Changing kick height or torso direction as well would mix the effects. We'll hold the model, camera and main poses fixed and change just the timing.

scenes.title: 핵심 자세가 지나가는 시간을 지키기
lines: A pose we deliberately specify is a keyframe. The other frames in the motion can be in-betweens. A coiled torso and an extended leg establish what the movement means. Intermediate poses connect those landmarks. Spending too long on that connection can blur both preparation and strike. Decide how long to read the preparation and the impact, then time the space between them. A bigger twist or extension can also increase the contrast between key poses. Let's take the timing we saw in the kick and apply it to a punch. Now the starting position and return path matter too.

scenes.title: 세 자세를 연결하는 것만으로는 부족하다
lines: Break an uppercut into three poses. The body lowers, the fist rises, and the arm extends upward. In Smash, the flash of a heavy hit gives way to an extended arm. Follow the outline after the effect clears. Showing a handful of drawings in sequence lets each distinct shape register. What if we fill the gaps in 3D, then play the same poses backward to return? A smooth transition can still lose the drive of the punch and its follow-through. Matching the drawings doesn't guarantee the same energy in motion.

scenes.title: 준비는 모으고 타격은 뻗기
lines: Look at the starting pose. Pulling the arm back gives the fist room to travel and makes its direction clear. Give the anticipation time to read and let the actual strike pass quickly. The striking phase might pass through three key poses in just one frame each. Distinct silhouettes and a clear impact can register even with little time on each pose. Every pose needn't stay on screen for an equal time. Give preparation and impact the timing each needs. Also check how the attack begins. A strike from a crouch starts differently from one that dips from standing. Preserve the starting state and the force the attack needs to convey.

scenes.title: 돌아오는 길도 공격의 일부다
lines: Let the extended fist return on a different path from the one it took upward. The hand comes closer to the body as the torso unwinds into the next action. That's a different movement from playing the punch backward. This trailing movement is called follow-through. It takes place before the character settles into idle. It shows how the body settles while the force of the attack is still present. Trace the outgoing and returning paths separately and the difference stands out. The hunter settles low under the sword after the swing. Removing that returning motion would lose some of its weight.

scenes.title: 보간을 게임의 리듬에 맞추기
lines: This doesn't make every move quick and short. When a character slowly lifts a heavy object, the intermediate motion is important information. Judge the motion by the feeling the game needs to convey. Interpolation is a convenient way to connect important poses. Give them time to read, and adjust the poses and the return path where needed. When a move feels sluggish, look at where it spends its time before speeding up the whole thing.
